label: September 1918
headline: The Line Breaks
deck: Americans take St Mihiel; the Allies storm the Hindenburg Line from the Meuse to the sea
caption: American infantry go forward through the shattered woods of the Argonne
body: On 12 September the First American Army under General Pershing attacks the St Mihiel salient with French troops at its side, and in two days the salient is gone. A fortnight later the Allied armies strike together from the Argonne to Flanders. On 29 September British troops cross the St Quentin Canal and break the Hindenburg Line.

In the Balkans the Allied army from Salonika breaks the Bulgarian front, and Bulgaria signs an armistice on 29 September. In Palestine the Turkish armies are routed at Megiddo and Damascus falls on 1 October.
Germany's new Chancellor, Prince Max of Baden, asks President Wilson for an armistice. Through October Cambrai, Lille and Ostend are taken, and Ludendorff is dismissed.
briefs: The mail boat Leinster is torpedoed in the Irish Sea; over five hundred die
Czechoslovakia proclaims its independence in Prague
Turkey signs an armistice at Mudros
